issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_cmp() Fails Identical keys
issue_context.body:

For build issues:

For other issues:

    If it isn't a build issue, example code or commands to reproduce
    the issue is highly appreciated.
    Also, please remember to tell us if you worked with your own
    OpenSSL build or if it is system provided.

Please remember to put ``` lines before and after any commands plus
output and code, like this:

    ```
    $ echo output output output
    output output output
    ```

    ```
    #include <stdio.h>
    
    int main() {
        int foo = 1;
        printf("%d\n", foo);
    }
    ```
-->
Create a EVP_PKEY and compare it to itself. EVP_PKEY_cmp() returns 0, which means a mismatch.
See code fragment below.

```
	int rv = 0;

	EVP_PKEY *mac_key = EVP_PKEY_new_raw_private_key(EVP_PKEY_HMAC, NULL,
	                                                 (const unsigned char *)("0123456789"),
	                                                 strlen("0123456789"));

    rv = EVP_PKEY_cmp(mac_key, mac_key);
    if (rv != 1) {
        printf("key compare failed. rv = %d\n", rv);
        return 0;
    }
    printf("key compare passed\n");
```


Possible fix ...
```
@ -130,8 +130,14 @@ int EVP_PKEY_cmp(const EVP_PKEY *a, const EVP_PKEY *b)
                return ret;
        }

        if (a->ameth->pub_cmp)
            return a->ameth->pub_cmp(a, b);
        if (a->ameth->pub_cmp) {
            ret = a->ameth->pub_cmp(a, b);
            if (ret == 0) {
                return 1;
            } else {
                return 0;
            }
        }
    }
```
The issue is present in the latest 1.1.1 stable branch. And appears to be on Master (3.0) as well.

Quote from https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.0/man3/EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD.html
---
The pub_cmp() method is called when two public keys are to be compared. It MUST return 1 when the keys are equal, 0 otherwise. It's called by EVP_PKEY_cmp(3).
---
Then see (1) hmac/hm_ameth.c and (2) ec/ec_ameth.c both pub_cmp does not follow documentation. The code in (2) is harmless in context of EVP_PKEY_cmp but in (1) is used ASN1_OCTET_STRING_cmp
Outside EVP_PKEY_cmp (2) must be considered as defect.


Quote from https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.0/man3/ASN1_STRING_cmp.html
---
ASN1_STRING_cmp() compares a and b returning 0 if the two are identical. The string types and content are compared.
---

Roumen

I see both on master and 1.1.1 that ec_ameth ec_key_pub_cmp returns 0 if EC_POINT_cmp() returns nonzero and 1 EC_POINT_cmp() returns 0. That is IMO correct.

The hmac implementation is broken. I'll submit PR for 1.1.1 (it is not there anymore in master at all).
I do not think it is relevant as EVP_PKEY_cmp is documented to have negative return values on errors.

And the pub_cmp() is not used outside of that call. And yeah, in theory you could obtain the ameth and obtain the pub_cmp() from it and call it directly from an application. Unless you have an example of such application I am not going to spend more time on that theoretical concern.
